lines: Hello Hannah, come on and take a seat. What do we like to talk about today? I'm not really sure where to start. I think I'm just anxious all the time and it's got worse in September. What happened in September?

I was my deputy head at my school. I've taught here for eleven years and I have love it. And then the head asked me to step up when our deputy left. That sounds like recognition of your work. That's what everyone says, but I keep thinking they picked the wrong person.

And that sooner or later someone will notice I have no idea what I'm doing. What does it look like when that thought arrives? Mostly Sunday evenings my chest goes tight and I start rehearsing Monday stuff meeting in my head. What do you rehearse?
Every possible question someone might ask and what I would say and what they would think of me if I got it wrong. What do you imagine they would think? That I'm out of my depth.

Day gave the joke to a nice E four teacher who can't actually read. Has anyone said anything that suggests that? No, just a strange thing. Nobody has. It's all in my head. It's still very real to you.

Very. Last week I rewrote the same email to the governors four times. Four times? What was the email about? Change to the behaviour policy. It was to Hargreaves. I was afraid Mr Hargreaves, the Chair of Governors, would think that I was stupid.

How does he treat you? He has been nothing but kind. He told me in September he was delighted. That makes it worse somehow because I feel like I'm lying to him. Lying to him about what? About being capable as if I'm pretending. Pretending to be what?

Uh, someone who knows what she's doing. Most days I feel like a child wearing her mother's coat. That's a little bit too much. Whose coat is that? My mom's, I suppose. She was a director for twenty years. Tell me about that.
Uh, she was brilliant. Everyone in the village still stops me say what a wonderful pet she was. She retired six years ago and they have named a library after her. And you know, in a similar job.

A deputy's job, but yes, I can't help comparing. Everything I do, I think, would she have done it better? Does she say that? Never. She is very supportive on the surface. She says I've always worried too much and I should stop being silly.
How does it blink when she says that? It makes me feel like I'm making a fuss so I don't tell her how bad it is. What does she not know? That I'm awake at four every morning. I fall asleep fine.
Then I'm awake to go through the to-do list. What is on the list? Everything. Timetable changes. The offset prep. A parent complaint. A child I'm worried about. It goes around and around.

How long have you been waking like that? Since about the second week of term. I drink a lot of coffee to get through a day, which I know doesn't help. How many cups? Five or six. Then I can't sit still in the afternoons.

What do you notice in your body during those hot minutes? My heart goes fast. My hands are a bit shaky. Last Thursday I had to leave a meeting to splash my face with water. Did anyone notice? I didn't think so. I said I was fetching a document.
It sounds like a lot of effort to hide it. It is. I'm exhausted by the end of every day just from pretending. Who knows how you're feeling? My partner Ben knows a bit.
He says I should just enjoy it. How do you feel when he says that? Guilty and a bit alone. He means well. He's an engineer. He thinks if something's a problem, you fix it.
You can't just say this. No, I wish it were that simple. Defense. Defense is cool. I'm talking. Not anymore, not really. I used to eat lunch in the year fourth quarter with the address.
No, I'm their line manager and it's all right. So it was some company along with the promotion? Yes, I hadn't thought of it like that. I missed them. I missed my class too. What do you miss most?

The children mostly. The day limit where a child gets something for the first time. No, my days are spreadsheets. Do you want a day promotion? I thought I did. I said yes in Durham because I couldn't say no to her.
Dad. Uh, then I went home and cried. What word terror is about? A year, I think. And that I would never get to go back. Will you go back? I don't know.

That sounds terrible, doesn't it? After everything's been so supportive. It sounds like an honest question. Nobody has asked me that. They just say well done. When was the last time you felt properly relaxed?

These summer holidays. We went walking in the lakes and I didn't think about school once for ten days. What is different here? Nobody expected anything of me. I was just walking. Ben carried the sandwiches.

And then? The week before term I was a wreck again. I couldn't eat on Sunday. Is there anything you already tried to help? You know, let me. I started writing down what went well each evening. Small things. A chill laughing. A good evening.

How did that go? It held for about two weeks and then I stopped because I felt so bad. So what? I am bragging to myself in a notebook. Not the same. What went well? That's not the same. That's bragging.

Probably not. It just felt that way. Some words back coming in, Cateria. Have you got a boat? Wondering if there is something particular you would like from our work? I would like to do the job without feeling like a frog.

What did that look like on a Tuesday? Mm. Working into a meeting and not rehearsing at first. Sending an email once. And on Sunday? Being able to sit on the sofa in the evening without my stomach in nox.
Those are clear goals. How did it feel now? I was saying, Demo, vote. Lightful. Lighter. A bit tearful, actually. That's right. Take a moment.
Sorry, I didn't expect that. There is nothing to apologize for. What's coming out? It's the first time I have told anyone how bad it is. Not even Ben knows how about it for me.
What would it be like to tell him? Scary. You would probably be hurt if I didn't say sooner. Would it be a reason to keep it to yourself?
I suppose not. I might try this week. What would help you do that? If I choose a quiet moment, not.

On a Sunday evening. Then I'm too hummed up. Saturday morning? Reps? Yeah, for breakfast. He's always in good mood then. And memories of the old thing. Would you try the evening notebook again just for a week? Even one line?
I could. I will put it by the kettle so I don't forget. All right, we're nearly out of time. Is there anything you want to add? Only did I nearly cancel this morning. I'm glad I didn't.
I'd like to. Same time, next week. Yes, please. Thank you.
